title: End-to-End Semi-Supervised Object Detection with Soft Teacher
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

problem.summary: Label acquisition is a bottleneck for detection, and prior pseudo-label semi-supervised detectors train in multiple stages, so their final accuracy is capped by pseudo labels produced by an initially weak detector trained on little labeled data.
statements: Annotation is a time-consuming and expensive bottleneck for scaling up training data.
Multi-stage pseudo-label methods train an initial detector on a small labeled set, then pseudo-label and re-train, so pseudo-label quality limits final performance.
Pseudo-labeling for detection is harder than for classification because annotations contain both location and category.
A high foreground-score threshold needed for precise positive pseudo labels leaves many true foreground candidates mislabeled as background.
Foreground score does not reliably indicate localization accuracy, so score-filtered pseudo boxes are unsuitable for training box regression.

evidence.quote: However, obtaining labels can be a bottleneck, due to the time-consuming and expensive annotation process.
the final performance is limited by the quality of pseudo labels generated by an initial and probably inaccurate detector trained using a small amount of labeled data.
creating pseudolabel for object detection is more complicated since an image usually contains multiple objects and the annotation of objects consists of location and category
However, while the strict criteria (higher threshold) leads to higher foreground precision, the recall of the retained box candidates also falls off quickly.
the localization accuracy and the foreground score of the box candidates do not show a strong positive correlation

background.summary: The work builds on pseudo-label based semi-supervised detection (STAC, Proposal Learning, Self-training) and consistency methods, adopting Mean-Teacher EMA updates and FixMatch-style weak/strong augmentation; the claimed gap is that all leading pseudo-label methods follow multi-stage training, and none uses the teacher to softly weight student losses.

solution.summary: An end-to-end teacher-student framework in which an EMA teacher pseudo-labels weakly augmented unlabeled images on the fly while the student trains on mixed labeled/unlabeled batches with strong augmentation; a soft teacher weights each background box's classification loss by the teacher's reliability score, and box jittering picks reliable pseudo boxes for regression via low box-regression variance.
solution.approach: Replace multi-stage pseudo-labeling with online teacher-student training whose pseudo boxes are softly weighted for classification and variance-filtered for regression.
components: mixed batches of labeled and unlabeled images sampled with a ratio sr, loss L = Ls + alpha*Lu
teacher model as exponential moving average (EMA) of the student, updated each iteration
soft teacher: teacher background score r_j normalizes the weight of each background box's classification loss
box jittering: jitter each pseudo box N times, refine with the teacher, and use regression variance as localization reliability
separate pseudo-box sets for classification (foreground-score filtered) and for regression (variance filtered at 0.02)
weak augmentation for teacher pseudo-labeling, strong augmentation for student training, following FixMatch

evidence.quote: This paper presents an end-to-end semi-supervised object detection approach, in contrast to previous more complex multi-stage methods.
a soft teacher mechanism where the classification loss of each unlabeled bounding box is weighed by the classification score produced by the teacher network
a box jittering approach to select reliable pseudo boxes for the learning of box regression
This end-to-end approach avoids the complicated multi-stage training scheme.
the teacher model is an exponential moving average (EMA) of the student model
we assess the reliability of each studentgenerated box candidate to be a real background, which is then used to weigh its background classification loss.
A smaller box regression variance indicates a higher localization reliability.

experiments.summary: Evaluated on MS-COCO under the Partially Labeled (1/5/10% of train2017) and Fully Labeled (train2017 + unlabeled2017) protocols with Faster R-CNN/FPN and stronger HTC++ (Swin-L) detectors, comparing against STAC and other SOTA, plus ablations of end-to-end vs multi-stage, soft teacher, box jittering, reliability indicators and thresholds on the 10% fold.

benchmarks.split: val2017, full train2017 + unlabeled2017, Faster R-CNN R50 (vs 40.9 supervised)
val2017, full labels, Faster R-CNN R101 (vs 43.8 supervised)
val2017 ablation, end-to-end + EMA + soft teacher + box jittering, 10% labels

evidence.quote: our method outperforms the STAC by 6.5 points, 6.4 points and 5.4 points when there are 1%, 5%, and 10% labeled data, respectively.
it can improve a 40.9 mAP baseline detector trained using the full COCO training set by +3.6 mAP, reaching 44.5 mAP, by leveraging the 123K unlabeled images of COCO.
which is the first work to surpass 60 mAP on COCO object detection benchmark.
By simply switching from the multi-stage framework to our end-to-end framework, performance is increased by 1.3 points.
integrating the soft teacher improves the performance by 2.4 points.

limitations.summary: There is no dedicated limitations section; evident constraints are strong sensitivity to the foreground-score and variance thresholds, heavy dependence on teacher-produced reliability signals (student scores hurt accuracy), extra per-box jittering computation, and evaluation restricted to MS COCO with a few detector families.
items: Performance is sensitive to the foreground threshold: values other than 0.9 cause significant degradation.
Reliability weighting must come from the teacher; using the student's own background score sharply hurts accuracy (25.9 vs 33.6 mAP).
Computing box-regression variance for all pseudo boxes is too costly, so only boxes with foreground score above 0.5 are considered.
Experiments cover only MS COCO; no other detection datasets are reported.

futureDirections.direction: Extend the end-to-end framework to single-stage detectors as well as two-stage ones (claimed applicable but only Faster R-CNN/HTC++ are evaluated).
futureDirections.quote: In theory, our framework is applicable to mainstream object detectors, including single-stage object detectors [15, 17, 21, 30] and two-stage object detectors [22, 9, 5, 35, 34].
